tier_reason: docs/src/bench.md (generated 2026-04-16 by the public bench/bench.sh and bench/build.sh, hyperfine 20 runs after 5 warmups) shows every claimed number against WAMR iwasm 2.4.3, wasm3 v0.5.1 and wasmi 2.0.0-beta.2, but it states no CPU model and no compiler versions, so it stays first-party tier C. The independent, fully specified harness rebeckerspecialties/wasm-benchmark (docs/runtime-comparison-2026-09-22.md, M4 Max E-cores, all build flags listed) does not confirm a win: wasmz geomean 1.59 vs wasm3 1.01 and WAMR 1.63 on M4 E-cores, and 1.63 vs WAMR 1.38 on iPhone XS (A12).

corrections.compiler_and_flags: wasmz dev built with 'make release' (Zig ReleaseFast); wasm3 at submodule commit 79d412e built with cmake (its CMakeLists defaults to Release, -O3); WAMR at submodule commit 11eb206 built with cmake -DWAMR_BUILD_INTERP=1 -DWAMR_BUILD_AOT=0 -DWAMR_BUILD_FAST_JIT=0 -DWAMR_BUILD_JIT=0 -DWAMR_BUILD_SIMD=0; wasmi at commit 9f6ff82 built with cargo build --release -p wasmi_cli (all in bench/build.sh). Compiler versions (Zig, gcc, rustc) are not stated in the report.
corrections.caveats: First-party numbers from a 2026-04-16 dev build; CPU model and compiler versions not stated. The wasm3 used is v0.5.1 (submodule commit 79d412e); the independent harness used v0.9.0. Timings are whole-process wall time via hyperfine, so start-up is included and wasmz's lazy (on first call) compilation favours it on the 19 MB esbuild module; WAMR is excluded from esbuild. The harness does not check program output. Many miscompilation fixes landed after the benchmark (August 2026 commits such as 'keep operand-stack reads of a local independent of later writes' and 'only rename a label slot onto the temporary that a branch consumes'), so the numbers were measured on code later fixed for correctness bugs. The QuickJS and esbuild memory rows measure the sh -c wrapper (1.8 MB for every runtime), so those RSS figures are invalid. The independent harness rebeckerspecialties/wasm-benchmark (docs/runtime-comparison-2026-09-22.md, wasmz v0.1.4) puts wasmz behind wasm3 (geomean 1.59 vs 1.01 on M4 Max E-cores). It is roughly level with WAMR fast-interp there (1.63) but behind it on iPhone XS A12 (1.63 vs 1.38), and ahead of wasmtime Pulley (2.09). The same harness reports six failing rows for wasmz: wrong results on extconst_init and extconst_init.mvp, traps on graphql_as and callref_dispatch, and segfaults on v128 ops in sieve and crc32. It also notes that wasmz never collects GC structs and does not support multi-memory or multi-value results through its C API. Treat the win over WAMR and wasm3 as unconfirmed. Zig library with a C API (libwasmz plus wasmz.h), so callable from C++.

notes: Claimed numbers match docs/src/bench.md exactly; README claim 'currently the fastest WebAssembly interpreter I have tested' confirmed verbatim. Metadata checked on github.com: MIT, 83 stars, not a fork, last commit 2026-08-17 (active). Shortcomings to record: first-party only with no CPU model; numbers predate August 2026 miscompilation fixes; an A-grade independent harness shows it 1.6x slower than wasm3 v0.9.0 and behind WAMR on A12, with 6 failing rows (wrong results, traps, crashes); RSS rows for QuickJS and esbuild measure the shell wrapper.

tier_reason: The README and docs/benchmarks.md (generated 2026-10-02 by the public bench/run.py) show all claimed numbers against wasmtime 49.0.1 Cranelift and Winch and wasmer 7.5.0 Cranelift and Singlepass on an Apple M5, with each run's output checked against native. It falls short of A because the rustc version used for the measured build is not recorded: there is no rust-toolchain file, and the README says only 'developed on 1.98'. The numbers are first-party, from 5 runs on a machine 'shared with other work while measuring', so tier C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Compile-only (wall clock, median): regex.wasm (1.36 MB) wisp 16.3 ms vs wasmtime Winch 24.2 ms, wasmer Singlepass 31.5 ms, wasmtime Cranelift 71.6 ms, wasmer Cranelift 82.0 ms; json.wasm (0.19 MB) wisp 4.5 ms vs Winch 8.3, Singlepass 14.2, wasmtime Cranelift 16.0, wasmer Cranelift 28.8. End to end (whole process, seconds): fib 34 wisp 0.022 vs wasmtime Cranelift 0.024, Winch 0.031, wasmer Singlepass 0.028; raytrace 0.054 vs Winch 0.066; json 0.263 vs Winch 0.325; regex 0.308 vs Winch 0.341. Slower than Winch on primes (0.120 vs 0.070), matmul (0.056 vs 0.049) and compress (0.713 vs 0.517), and 1.5-2.5x slower than wasmtime Cranelift on six of seven programs.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: wisp: cargo build --release (Cargo.toml release profile with debug = 1; rustc version not recorded for the run, README says developed on 1.98). Guest programs: cargo build --release --target wasm32-wasip1. Baselines: wasmtime 49.0.1 and wasmer 7.5.0 release binaries run with -C cache=n / --disable-cache, Winch via -C compiler=winch (bench/run.py).
corrections.hardware: Apple M5, 10 cores, Darwin 27.0.0 (macOS 27); machine shared with other work while measuring
corrections.caveats: The README says plainly that wisp is 1.5-2.5x slower than wasmtime Cranelift end to end on six of seven programs (only fib is faster, 0.022 vs 0.024 s, within noise). It also loses to Winch on primes, compress and matmul. The compile-time comparison is not like for like: wasmtime and wasmer compile functions in parallel and write the artefact to disk, while wisp compiles single-threaded in one process. All timings are whole-process wall clock (start-up included), median of only 5 runs, on a machine shared with other work. Own benchmarks only, 0 stars, 15 commits made 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-02, very new. The compiler runs only on AArch64 macOS (Linux/AArch64 paths are untested and disabled; other hosts use the interpreter, which is 3-8x slower than the compiler). No SIMD, threads or Wasm 3.0 proposals. A Rust library with no C API header yet, so not callable from C++ without bindings.

notes: Numbers match the README and docs/benchmarks.md; added the json.wasm compile-only rows and the losing rows to claimed_speedup. Metadata checked on github.com: MIT (LICENSE and Cargo.toml), 0 stars, 0 forks, not a fork, last commit 2026-10-02 (active). Benchmarks were rerun on the final code ('bench: rerun on the final code'); only an interpreter NaN-rounding fix came after. Shortcomings to record: wins only on compile time and against Winch on 4 of 7 programs; compile comparison not like for like; first-party, 5 runs on a shared machine, rustc version unrecorded; compiler limited to AArch64 macOS; no C API.
